text.text: Book of the Month: Klara and the Sun

:books: *_Klara and the Sun_* by Kazuo Ishiguro

What does it mean to love someone — and can a machine truly understand that question? Ishiguro's first novel since winning the Nobel Prize is a quietly devastating story told through the eyes of an AI companion. It's tender, strange, and will change how you think about consciousness.

:calendar: *Key Dates*
• Reading deadline: March 20, 2026
• Discussion session: March 22, 2026 at 12:00 PM

:brain: *Did you know?*
• Ishiguro wrote this partly as a companion to _Never Let Me Go_, exploring what makes us human from the opposite direction — through an artificial being looking in.
• Klara describes the visual world in geometric terms, as though processing images through sensors rather than eyes.
• The book was written under enormous pressure — it was Ishiguro's first novel after the Nobel Prize, and he described the expectations as "paralyzing."
